topic: Ind AS 10: Events after Reporting Period
title: Events After
simple_words: Something happens after the year-end but before accounts are approved. Ask: did it prove a year-end condition, or is it new?

definitions.meaning: Favourable or unfavourable events between the end of the reporting period and the date the financial statements are approved for issue.
definitions.note: Window ends at approval date, not AGM date

definitions.meaning: Event giving evidence of conditions that existed at the end of the reporting period. Amounts in the statements are changed.

key_points: ==Adjusting events==: evidence of conditions existing at the reporting date; recognised amounts are changed.
==Non-adjusting events==: conditions arose after the reporting date; only disclosed if material.
!!Dividends declared after the reporting period are not recognised as a liability at that date!!; disclose them.
If going concern no longer holds after the period, accounts are not prepared on a going concern basis (adjusting in effect).
formula_hook: sort every event into a box

rows: Customer insolvent after year-end, owed old debt
Court case settled, existing obligation at year-end
Fraud or error found, shows statements wrong
Fall in market value of investments after year-end

insight.text: Adjust only if the event confirms a condition that already existed on the reporting date; new conditions are disclosed.

memory_trick.explanation: If the cause is old (existed at year-end), adjust. If the cause is new (arose after year-end), only disclose. Think of a fire: new cause, so disclose.

steps: Did the condition exist at year-end?
exam_tip: Use the approval date by the board for issue as the cut-off. Always state the reason for adjusting or not adjusting in your answer.

doubt.question: Dividend declared after year-end: why no liability?
doubt.answer: There is no present obligation at the reporting date, since the dividend was not declared then. So it is not recognised; it is disclosed.

mistakes.wrong: Adjusting for a fire loss that happened after year-end
mistakes.right: It is a non-adjusting event; disclose nature and financial effect if material.

mistakes.wrong: Recognising proposed dividend after year-end as a liability
mistakes.right: No liability at the reporting date; disclose the dividend in the notes.

mistakes.wrong: Treating the AGM date as the end of the event window
mistakes.right: The window ends on the date the financial statements are approved for issue.

Checker 1: Step 5 ('No: disclose nature and estimate'): this is incomplete and should say when disclosure is needed. Correct version: 'No: if material, disclose the nature of the event and an estimate of its financial effect, or state that such an estimate cannot be made (Ind AS 10, para 21).'

Checker 1: Key point 4 ('adjusting in effect'): this wording is loose. Ind AS 10 (paras 14–15) says the effect is pervasive. It calls for a fundamental change in the basis of accounting, not just an adjustment of recognised amounts. Suggested wording: 'If, after the reporting period, management decides to liquidate or stop trading, or has no realistic alternative, the statements shall not be prepared on a going concern basis. This is a change of basis, not a mere adjustment.'

Checker 1: Table row 4 and the memory trick (fire = disclose): add a caveat. A non-adjusting event can still be serious enough to remove the going concern assumption. In that case the treatment in para 14 applies, not just disclosure.
